passages.text: I, Clement, am a Roman citizen, and I have been able to live my early life with self-control, because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied with dejection and distress. For a thought concerning death stayed with me—I do not know where it got its start—repeatedly reminding me that, once dead, I do not exist and no one will ever make mention of me, as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion. And I shall be one who is not, knowing those who are not, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, not coming into being. And did the world ever come into being, and before it came into being, what was there? For if it always existed, it will also exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what will there be in turn, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Ῥωμαίων πολίτης ὢν
lexical_decisions.chosen: am a Roman citizen
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the conventional English description while preserving Clement’s stated civic identity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν πρώτην ἡλικίαν σωφρόνως ζῆσαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: live my early life with self-control
lexical_decisions.rationale: σωφρόνως denotes restrained or temperate conduct, while πρώτη ἡλικία refers to the earliest period of life.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the genitive absolute causally and preserves the image of the inward desire being kept occupied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the personification of time and the emphatic πάντων τὰ πάντα.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: I shall be one who is not, knowing those who are not
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering construes οὐκ directly with ὄντας, making the substantival participle the object of εἰδώς. A possible wider scope for the negation would instead yield “not knowing those who exist”; the intended scope remains uncertain.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τάχα ἔσται τι ὃ νῦν νοῆσαι οὐ δυνατόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived
lexical_decisions.rationale: νοῆσαι concerns mental conception or apprehension, and καί continues the preceding sequence.

source_issues.issue: The supplied wording permits at least two interpretations of the negation’s scope. Taking οὐκ with ὄντας gives “knowing those who are not,” as in the main text. Taking the preceding negation with wider scope over the participial expression may give “not knowing those who exist.” The masculine plural also has no explicit antecedent. The surrounding catalogue does not decisively establish the intended interpretation. This is an unresolved scope-and-meaning problem in the supplied reading, not a demonstrated transcription error or source corruption.

passages.text: Constantly pondering these and similar things—I do not know from where—I had such painful grief that, having grown pale, I wasted away. Most terrible of all, if I ever resolved to thrust the concern away as useless, the affliction became all the more acute for me. I was distressed at this, not knowing that I had a beautiful thought as a housemate, one that would become for me the cause of a good immortality, as I later learned by experience and thanked God, the Master of all. For by the thought that distressed me at first, I was compelled to come to the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπαύστως ἐνθυμούμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: constantly pondering
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys both the uninterrupted recurrence and the inwardly reflective character of ἐνθυμέομαι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὀδυνηρὰν εἶχον λύπην τοσοῦτον ὡς ὠχριακότα με τήκεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: I had such painful grief that, having grown pale, I wasted away
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the degree construction and represents ὠχριακότα as prior or accompanying pallor rather than omitting it.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀκμαιότερόν μοι μᾶλλον τὸ πάθος ἐγίνετο
lexical_decisions.chosen: the affliction became all the more acute for me
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀκμαιότερον describes the condition as growing stronger or more intense.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σύνοικον καλὴν ἔχων ἔννοιαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: I had a beautiful thought as a housemate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the domestic image of the thought dwelling together with Clement.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀθανασίας ἀγαθῆς αἰτίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the cause of a good immortality
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the explicit qualification ἀγαθῆς, which may distinguish beneficial immortality from an enduring harmful state.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον
lexical_decisions.chosen: I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the deliberate opposition between ταλανίζω and μακαρίζω.

passages.text: From childhood, then, while occupied with such thoughts, I frequented the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing else there but doctrines being torn down and built up, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time, for example, the position that the soul is immortal prevailed; at another, the position that it is mortal. So whenever an argument that it was immortal prevailed, I rejoiced; but whenever one that it was mortal prevailed, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I was unable to establish either alternative as certain in my own mind. Still, I understood that opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them and do not appear as they actually stand with respect to truth. Having therefore at last recognized that a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended, but that opinions are pronounced on the basis of those defending them, I was reeling still more amid these matters. That is why I groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither able to establish anything as certain, nor could I shake off concern for such matters, although I wanted to, as I said earlier: when I more frequently ordered myself to be still, the thought of such things would, I do not know how, enter me unnoticed and with pleasure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς
lexical_decisions.chosen: I frequented the philosophers’ schools
lexical_decisions.rationale: διατριβαί here denotes places or circles of philosophical instruction rather than casual conversation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δογμάτων ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς
lexical_decisions.chosen: doctrines being torn down and built up
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the paired destructive and constructive imagery rather than reducing it to generic disagreement.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: συλλογισμῶν τέχνας καὶ λημμάτων ἐπινοίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises
lexical_decisions.rationale: λήμματα are propositions or premises adopted in argument, while τέχναι emphasizes methodical argumentative techniques.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἴ ποτε οὖν ἐπεκράτει λόγος ὅτι ἀθάνατος, ἔχαιρον
lexical_decisions.chosen: So whenever an argument that it was immortal prevailed, I rejoiced
lexical_decisions.rationale: “So” explicitly preserves the inferential οὖν connecting Clement’s response with the preceding alternation of successful arguments.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them
lexical_decisions.rationale: παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας makes the advocates, rather than the intrinsic merits of the theses, the basis of the assessment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ παρὰ τὰς ἐκδικουμένας ὑποθέσεις ἡ κατάληψις γίνεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατάληψις is used in a philosophical context for apprehension or secure cognitive grasp.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔτι μᾶλλον ἰλιγγίων ἐν τοῖς πράγμασιν. διὸ ἐκ τοῦ τῆς ψυχῆς βάθους ἐστέναζον
lexical_decisions.chosen: I was reeling still more amid these matters. That is why I groaned from the depth of my soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats ἰλιγγίων as the finite imperfect and preserves the independent assertion followed by the explicit consequence marked by διό.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐμαυτῷ πυκνότερον ἡσυχάζειν ἐπιτάσσοντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: when I more frequently ordered myself to be still
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the comparative force of πυκνότερον. The participial subject is unexpressed in the Greek and is understood contextually as Clement.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λανθανόντως μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς ὁ τῶν τοιούτων μοι εἰσήρχετο λογισμός
lexical_decisions.chosen: the thought of such things would ... enter me unnoticed and with pleasure
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the stealth conveyed by λανθανόντως and the expressly pleasurable quality conveyed by μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς.

passages.text: Again, at a loss, I said to myself, “Why am I laboring in vain? The matter is clear: if, once dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. Therefore I will reserve grieving for that time, when, not existing, I shall not grieve. But if, after all, I am something, then my grieving now is superfluous.” Immediately after this, another thought entered me, for I said, “Unless, indeed, because I have not lived devoutly, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, and according to the accounts of certain philosophers I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and shall be in Hades, punished for all time.” Again I countered, saying, “But there are no such things.” And again I said, “But what if there are? Since the matter is uncertain, then,” I said, “it is safer instead for me to live devoutly. And how will I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the pleasures of the body? But I have not even been fully assured of what exactly is right and pleasing to God; nor do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal, nor what reliable account can be found, nor am I able to rest from such thoughts.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Τί ματαιοπονῶ;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Why am I laboring in vain?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the image of expending effort fruitlessly.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will reserve grieving for that time
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats τὴν τότε as an elliptical reference to the future time under discussion without presenting an unstated noun as part of the Greek.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα εἰμί τι
lexical_decisions.chosen: if, after all, I am something
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the deliberately indefinite τι, allowing the possibility of continued existence in some unspecified state.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω, μὴ βεβιωκὼς εὐσεβῶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Unless, indeed, because I have not lived devoutly, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now
lexical_decisions.rationale: Reads εἰ μήτι γε exceptively, as qualifying the preceding reassurance that present grief is superfluous. It can alternatively be heard as an apprehensive question, “What if, indeed, I am to suffer there something worse ...?”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Πυριφλεγέθοντι καὶ Ταρτάρῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus
lexical_decisions.rationale: Transliterates the named mythological places rather than replacing them with generalized terms.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν ᾅδου τὸν αἰῶνα κολαζόμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: in Hades, punished for all time
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative of duration τὸν αἰῶνα portrays the punishment as enduring throughout the age or indefinitely; “for all time” preserves that force without importing a separate doctrinal formulation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀδήλου οὖν ὄντος τοῦ πράγματος (ἔλεγον) ἀκινδυνότερόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον εὐσεβῶς βιῶσαί με
lexical_decisions.chosen: Since the matter is uncertain, then,” I said, “it is safer instead for me to live devoutly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Restores the parenthetical ἔλεγον as a repeated reporting clause and renders μᾶλλον as the preference “instead” or “rather.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ δικαίου χάριν
lexical_decisions.chosen: for the sake of what is right
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized neuter refers to what is right or just rather than necessarily invoking a technical doctrine of righteousness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίς λόγος βέβαιος εὑρίσκεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: what reliable account can be found
lexical_decisions.rationale: λόγος may denote an argument, explanation, or account here; “account” leaves that scope open while βέβαιος conveys dependability.
